newsitem.title: USA: US says job exposure to lead is down, but continues.
newsitem.headline: US says job exposure to lead is down, but continues.

text.p: Blood samples from workers in 25 states have shown a decline in the levels of lead, but federal health officials said Thursday that work-related exposure to lead remains a problem.

The U.S. Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) said there was a 15 percent decrease in elevated blood lead levels detected by surveillance laboratories among adults during July, August and September 1996.

The agency said it could not determine if the decline was because of decreased occupational exposure to lead or meant that fewer workers were undergoing blood lead monitoring required by the Occupational Safety and Health Administration.

Construction workers can be exposed to lead when they disturb or remove lead paint or work in industries such as battery and solder manufacturing or lead smelting. Lead poisoning can have reproductive and neurological effects on workers.
